details.description: GPT-4o transcribe is OpenAI's speech-to-text model built on GPT-4o, used through the Transcription API (/v1/audio/transcriptions) and still labeled Preview in Azure's Foundry Models catalog. OpenAI's model page states it improves on the original Whisper model's word error rate and language recognition; OpenAI's current speech-to-text guide now directs new general-purpose transcription integrations to gpt-transcribe instead. On August 26, 2026, OpenAI notified developers that gpt-4o-transcribe, alongside whisper-1, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, will be removed from the API on February 26, 2027, recommending gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe as replacements.
advantages: OpenAI states it improves on the original Whisper model's word error rate and language recognition, per OpenAI's model page.
Existing integrations support a free-text prompt to improve recognition of names, acronyms and recording-specific vocabulary, per OpenAI's speech-to-text guide.
Supports file streaming for transcription integrations, per OpenAI's speech-to-text guide.
disadvantages: OpenAI has deprecated gpt-4o-transcribe, announcing on August 26, 2026 that it will be removed from the API on February 26, 2027, with gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe recommended as replacements, per OpenAI's deprecations page.
Azure's Foundry Models catalog still labels this model Preview, per Microsoft's models page.
Available only through the Transcription and Realtime endpoints; does not support Chat Completions, Assistants or Speech Generation, per OpenAI's model page.
Knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2024, per OpenAI's model page.
use_cases: Transcribing recorded speech into text via the Transcription API, per OpenAI's model page.
General-purpose speech-to-text transcription positioned by OpenAI as an alternative to Whisper, per OpenAI's model page.

notes: OpenAI's deprecations page gives a shutdown date of February 26, 2027 for gpt-4o-transcribe, which differs from the catalog's 2026-10-15 deprecation_date; kept the catalog's date as instructed but flagging the conflict since it affects whether the model is still callable on that date. No source states which specific languages gpt-4o-transcribe supports (only whisper-1 and the separate gpt-transcribe model's language handling are documented), so the languages list is left empty. Verification pass: OpenAI's current speech-to-text guide gives the 'recommended, general-purpose model for transcribing recorded speech in its original language' framing, and the structured 'keywords' prompting parameter, to gpt-transcribe, not gpt-4o-transcribe (gpt-4o-transcribe only gets a free-text prompt) -- both were corrected. OpenAI's model page also shows the Realtime endpoint (v1/realtime), not just Transcription, as supported for gpt-4o-transcribe, so the endpoint disadvantage was corrected to not claim it is limited to Transcription alone.
